title: The fixed charge changes the bill
hook: A lower per-kWh price can still produce a higher total at small usage.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare fixed and usage-dependent charges in a stated bill model.

misconception: The smallest per-kWh rate always makes the smallest total bill.
objective: Compare fixed and usage-dependent charges in a stated bill model.

claims.text: Fictional tariff A is €0.20/kWh plus €10. B is €0.30/kWh without a fixed charge. Scaled model; fictional:€0.20/kWh+€10;€0.30/kWh;no taxes.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Usage=40kWh, A=€18 and B=€12. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",["*","x",0.2],10]; B=["*","x",0.3]; x denotes Usage. At x=40, A=18, B=12. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A lower variable rate does not erase a fixed charge. At 40kWh, A totals €18 and B €12. They match at 100kWh under these exact assumptions; real tariffs can include other terms.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",["*","x",0.2],10]; B=["*","x",0.3]; x denotes Usage. At x=40, A=18, B=12. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Fictional tariff A is €0.20/kWh plus €10; tariff B is €0.30/kWh with no fixed charge. Above what usage is A's bill lower? Correct: 100kWh. A's €10 fixed charge is recovered at €0.10 per kWh saved, so the bills match at 100kWh; below that, B is lower.

claims.text: For a stated constant load, kWh = watts × hours ÷ 1000. Running cost = kWh × the stated price per kWh; stated fixed costs are added separately.
claims.source: https://www.energy.gov.au/households/energy-rating Australian Government, Energy Ratings, sections Electrical appliances without a star rating / Estimate running costs. Opened 2026-10-13. This supports the general calculation, not the invented model ratings or tariff.
